newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end lower after week long run-up.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end lower after week long run-up.

text.p: French shares closed in negative ground after racking up major gains this week, tracking Wall Street's welcome to Bill Clinton's return to the White House.

Domestic funds locked up some of their profits ahead of a long weekend and in anticipation of a Wall Street hangover to the week-long party, traders said. A softer tone in French bonds also served as a trigger to profit-taking here.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 6.61 points or 0.3 percent at 2,205.20, while on the week, the index advanced 3.02 percent.
The CAC-40 futures contract was down three at 2,210 from Thursday's close.
* Support for the CAC below the current level seen at 2,196, 2,183 and 2,169-92, while resistance was seen at 2,218, 2,232 and 2,261-63
* UAP gallops ahead, putting on 6.27 percent to 116.90 francs as persistent rumours of a bid by Axa send the stock soaring. Axa weakens 0.99 percent to 318.5.
* AGF rises 1.15 percent to 157.8 francs in sympathy, while BNP shakes off initial weakness. BNP would take a capital loss on its UAP stake if Axa made a bid.
* Renault eases 2.44 percent to 119.90 francs, returning to its level before the stock saw significant buying on Thursday from Morgan Stanley.

* Among a handful of CAC-40 stocks which rose more than one percent were Rhone-Poulenc up three francs to 158, Promodes up 28 to 1,522, Peugeot up six to 567, Michelin up 2.8 to 260.3 and Lagardere up 1.2 to 162.
* Pernod Ricard down 2.13 percent to 280 francs, continuing to suffer from its forecast that the French spirits market will fall two/three percent in 1997 due to tax increases.
* Dassault group companies please. Dassault Aviation climbs 3.94 percent to 1,160. The company expects the 1996 profit to reflect the rise in first half pretax pre-exceptional profit.
Dassault Electronique firms 6.24 percent to 477, while Dassault Systemes advances 5.29 percent to 249
* Cetelem rises 5.65 percent to 1,215 on hopes of a buy-out from parent Cie Bancaire or Paribas. The stock was also seen ripe for catching up on the market rise
